title: Better Semiconductor Stock to Buy: Broadcom or Qualcomm? | AVGO Stock vs. QCOM Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garble some words and the sponsor name in places
summary: Parkevtate compares Broadcom and Qualcomm head-to-head; he owns both and wants to add to each, so the question is which to buy first. On earnings prospects, Broadcom's expected EPS growth has surged to 55%, driven by its custom-chip business helping companies such as Alphabet build proprietary chips, with sales in the tens of billions, while Qualcomm's EPS expectations are muted because smartphones, its main profit source, are strained by higher component prices caused partly by AI demand. Qualcomm is diversifying well, he argues: automotive is booming, its chips for computers and laptops are doing well, and data-center orders already run into the billions and should become meaningful from the second half of 2027, which is why he opened the position. On margins, Broadcom leads with operating margins above 48% against Qualcomm's 21% and falling, though Qualcomm's return on invested capital is higher at 33% versus Broadcom's 26%. Both are asset-light, outsourcing manufacturing to TSMC. On valuation, Broadcom trades at a forward P/E of 10.6, its cheapest in years, against Qualcomm's 14.3, but his DCF fair values flip the ranking: $462 for Broadcom versus a $320 price (about 44% upside) and $279 for Qualcomm versus $175 (about 60% upside), so overall the valuation gap is negligible. He picks Broadcom, but calls it a close call and wants more of both. He also flags the Nvidia scandal, with Nvidia down over 5%, and notes Nvidia reports on 17 November, which he will cover live for channel members. Both stocks are BUY reiterations.
